**Attendees**: Marek Pillár (BigHub, PM Dr. Max account), Tereza Foltýnová (ViaPharma CZE, logistics)

## TL;DR

Marek and Tereza agreed the logistics Part A/B split. **Part A:** Marek takes over Reklamace documentation himself and makes it his main focus for the next ~2 weeks, ahead of Fakturace doprav, aiming for a near-final spec both sides can see. He is also Tereza's single point of contact for all logistics initiatives. **Part B:** Tereza fills in new logistics AI initiatives herself, using the 2-row BQ check table as a template on the shared ViaPharma SharePoint, and validates them with Petr Spilka and later Rudolf Žůrek. Next Friday's (2026-10-02) session is an internal validation debate, not a final version. Tereza also said openly that Reklamace's "agile, no full spec" approach has now backfired: only part of the process is described, and phases 3–5 haven't been touched.

- **From 2026-09-15**: the ~9 initiatives left over from the BQ interview are no longer handled in live sessions. Tereza drafts new initiatives herself in the tracker format, and Marek helps frame them on request. This replaces the deprioritized follow-up session.

## Key Discussion Points

### Reklamace: Marek takes over the documentation

Marek said he is 3–4 weeks into the account and still getting oriented on Reklamace. He had planned to spend Thursday–Friday and next week on Fakturace doprav. After the Reklamace discussions this week and Tereza's own read that the scope isn't closed, he has **moved his focus entirely to Reklamace**. The goal is a transparent, agreed document so that Filip Černý (developer) builds against something both sides have signed off. Marek told Tereza, and asked her to keep it between them, that he has taken all logistics initiatives under himself.

Marek framed the current blocker as a decision, not implementation. Whichever option the client picks for the supplier data (Axapta or an alternative) can be delivered relatively quickly. BigHub's job is to lay out pros and cons and a recommendation, and "the ball stays on your side" [translated from Slovak]. That options table is being prepared for the Thursday 2026-10-01 logistics status meeting (see [[ASM-169]]).

Tereza gave the client-side view of the process:
- Only part of the Reklamace process is described, "not even half".
- Phase 2 is partly worked out, but phases 3, 4 and 5 "haven't been touched".
- Scope "keeps swelling strangely".

Marek added that most of the real emails Jana Egrmaierová forwarded to Filip were edge cases: out of ~10, only ~2 were straightforward.

Tereza tied this directly to the delivery approach: "We said we didn't want it agile, but it was decided: let's do it agile, we'll keep refining it. And now it feels like it has bitten us, because it isn't finished" [translated from Czech]. She was also frustrated about the [previous day's session](2026-09-24-viapharma-reklamace-knowledge-base-standoff.md): "It bothers me all the more when we listened yesterday to 'it's exactly as it is in the specification' — we meet every Thursday, and there were never that many questions" [translated from Czech]. She let it go: "it can happen on any project".

Both agreed a spec is not dogma and changes on either side are fine. Tereza offered full support: "Jana knows a lot, Petr knows the most". Anything on Reklamace can be written up and a meeting set, and "every question is good... look where it has led us now" [translated from Czech].

**Fakturace doprav (dopravy)** is the other big topic. Tereza called it "in diapers", at the first phase, and largely driven by Honza Sovka so far. She is unsure whether it will become BigHub's topic, but expects it to need further description work.

### Tracker and Part B: new logistics initiatives

Marek confirmed that the tracker was reviewed with Tomáš Dudaško on 2026-09-24 and makes sense for both logistics projects. He noted the phase 1 / phase 2 split sketched by Jan Žižka (phase 1 in progress, phase 2 open). The longer-term goal, through November and year-end, is to collect further logistics initiatives: pain points, repetitive work and simplifications, each framed as a project. BigHub is allocated to Dr. Max in general, so initiatives with the biggest measurable savings for Dudaško get priority.

The agreed mechanics:
- **Template**: Tereza takes the 2-row BQ "check" table that went to Dudaško for approval and uses it as a template. She keeps the existing topics she wants to continue and describes new ones.
- **Location**: Tereza saved a copy to the shared ViaPharma–BigHub SharePoint. This is the working logistics table; once a cross-department master exists, the two get reconciled and the master becomes the single view. Marek now has access to the "SZE AI logistika" folder (via his external account). Tereza said it contains everything shared so far, including Jana's Reklamace material.
- **Master visibility**: Tereza asked whether a combined table showing other departments' initiatives exists. Marek has one and will ask Tomáš Dudaško whether it can be shared across departments.
- **Validation path**: Tereza must go through the table with **Petr Spilka** first, then with **Rudolf Žůrek**. Monday 2026-09-28 is a public holiday, and she can't get Spilka's time next week (already tried for Reklamace). She wants to keep **next Friday's session (2026-10-02)** but treat it as an **internal validation debate**, not a definitive version, and not yet with Žůrek. She described Spilka as "the owner of Reklamace, the main person for warehouses after Mr. Žůrek" [translated from Czech].
- **Framing help**: Marek offered async help (chat or a quick call) so the Friday version has more than one Excel row per topic: time bounds, priorities for both sides, and a better-framed problem and solution. They suggested Wednesday or Thursday to review her draft beforehand.
- Tereza will also look at the existing initiatives and see whether any can be removed or moved to the backlog.

### Logistics

- Tereza should email Marek at his **external (Dr. Max) account**. Invitations to his BigHub address have bounced. Marek has both mailboxes connected.
- **Wednesday 2026-09-30, 10:00**: 30-minute in-person catch-up at Florentinum (Tereza is sending the invite). Marek has a meeting 11:00–12:00.

## Decisions Made

- **Part A/B split agreed.** Part A: Marek owns the Reklamace documentation and makes it his main focus for the next ~2 weeks, ahead of Fakturace doprav, aiming for a near-final transparent spec. Part B: Tereza drafts new logistics initiatives herself in the tracker format, with Marek helping frame them on request.
- **Marek is the single point of contact** for all logistics AI initiatives on BigHub's side.
- **Logistics initiatives table**: Tereza's copy on the shared ViaPharma SharePoint, built from the 2-row check-table template, is the working logistics table until a cross-department master is shared. The two are then reconciled and the master becomes the single view.
- **2026-10-02 session** stays, but as an internal validation debate, not a final version. Validation order: Petr Spilka first, then Rudolf Žůrek.
- **Spec as a living document**: both sides agree the spec can change when either side needs it. Changes are raised openly at the weekly Thursday sync.

## Sentiment & Tone

Warm and constructive. Tereza was open about her frustration with Reklamace ("it has bitten us", the "exactly as in the spec" comment) but explicitly moved on. She sounded supportive, not adversarial: "every question is good". Compared with the 2026-09-23 "BigHub doesn't want to deliver" narrative, this is a clear improvement. Marek taking visible ownership of the documentation and becoming the single contact seems to land well; she proposed the in-person meeting herself. Watch-outs: she carries a lot of process knowledge but has limited reach to Spilka and Žůrek, which paces Part B. Her "we didn't want agile" framing may resurface if Reklamace scope keeps growing.
